metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 'Directions (none endorsed)' framing with AC1-AC4, which require the mandatory-check direction to be implemented and a decision recorded — state explicitly which direction is adopted.
evidence: Directions header: 'Directions (none endorsed; the ticket is the problem statement)'
AC4: 'Whichever direction is chosen is recorded with its reasoning, including an explicit decision on per-session identities (adopt or reject with a reason)'
AC1: 'by a documented and scripted check' — presupposes the third direction was built
findings.finding: The 'Directions' section states 'none endorsed; the ticket is the problem statement', but AC4 requires a chosen direction recorded with reasoning plus an explicit adopt/reject decision on per-session identities, and AC1-AC3 all presuppose the third direction (the mandatory scripted pre-submit check) was implemented. The section and the criteria point the implementer in two directions.
findings.location: 'Directions (none endorsed...)' section vs Acceptance criteria AC1-AC4
scenarios: An executor reads 'none endorsed' and produces only a problem statement, then fails AC1-AC4 which require a chosen, built, and recorded solution.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the Directions framing to name the adopted direction (the mandatory scripted pre-submit check) and record the per-session-identity reject reason, consistent with AC4.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the pre-submit check's failure mode (fail-closed: refuse the submit when the Gerrit/worktree query errors or times out) so a query failure cannot silently reopen the race.
evidence: Third direction: 'confirm current_revision matches what you inspected, confirm votes are live... check git worktree list' — all depend on a Gerrit/local query that can fail
Absence: no statement of behavior when the ownership/revision query errors or times out
findings.finding: The pre-submit check reads external state (Gerrit change metadata, current_revision, vote liveness) and local git worktree state, but the plan does not specify the check's own failure mode: if the Gerrit query fails or is unreachable, does the check fail-closed (block the submit) or fail-open (allow it)? A safety guard that fails open silently reintroduces the very race it guards against.
scenarios: Gerrit is slow/unreachable during preflight; a fail-open check waves the submit through and races another session's rebase — the exact 39-second hazard recurs.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to AC1/AC2: if the revision/ownership query errors or times out, the check exits non-zero and refuses the submit (fail-closed).

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the disposition of the stale-revision refusal — e.g. it is retryable: re-inspect the new current_revision and re-verify that LLM-Review/Verified votes are live before any re-submit.
evidence: AC2: 'A submit is refused, or at minimum loudly warned, when the current_revision differs' — no disposition word (retryable vs fatal) attached to the refusal
findings.finding: AC2 adds a new submit-refusal arm ('refused, or at minimum loudly warned' on stale current_revision) but does not state the caller-facing disposition of that refusal — whether a stale-revision refusal is retryable (re-inspect the fresh revision, re-verify votes, and possibly submit) or fatal (abandon the submit). Without an explicit disposition, an agent hitting the guard cannot tell whether to retry or stop.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether AC2 requires a hard refusal or a warning (state the default), and align the proof step accordingly.
evidence: AC2: 'A submit is refused, or at minimum loudly warned, when the current_revision differs...'
AC2 proof: 'observing the refusal' — presupposes refusal, not a warning
findings.finding: AC2 offers a disjunction — 'A submit is refused, or at minimum loudly warned' — without deciding which behavior is required. The proving method ('observe the refusal') assumes refusal, but the criterion also permits a mere warning, so the acceptance bar is ambiguous.
scenarios: Implementer ships only a warning; reviewer expected a hard refusal; the proof step ('observe the refusal') then cannot pass.
findings.suggested_fix: State: 'the script exits non-zero and refuses to submit when current_revision differs' as the required behavior, dropping the 'at minimum warned' fallback or moving it to a documented degraded mode.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the concrete script path and the doc file (the push-flow doc / AGENTS.md section) that AC1 and AC3 must land in, so the check and the vote-invalidation note are locatable.
evidence: AC1: 'by a documented and scripted check rather than by an agent happening to think of it'
AC3: 'stated wherever the push flow is documented'
Third direction: 'document (and script) the pre-submit verification' — no path given
findings.finding: The location of the documentation and the scripted check is undefined. AC1 requires 'a documented and scripted check' with no named script path/file; AC3 requires the vote-invalidation note stated 'wherever the push flow is documented' with no named doc. An executor cannot know which file to edit or where the script lives.
scenarios: Executor writes the check into an ad-hoc location that other sessions never read, so the guard is never invoked.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify e.g. 'scripts/gerrit-preflight.sh' and the exact push-flow doc (path) where the Outdated-vote warning is added.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the pre-submit check closes the check-then-act window — e.g. condition the Gerrit submit on the exact inspected revision-id so the submit fails atomically if current_revision advanced, rather than re-reading then submitting.
evidence: Plan: 'the check ran at 02:36:18' vs 'patch set 4 had been uploaded 39 seconds earlier (02:35:39)' — the original failure IS a check-then-act race
AC2 verifies current_revision at check time but does not bind the submit to that revision atomically
findings.finding: The endorsed acceptance-criteria mechanism (verify current_revision matches the inspected revision, then submit) is a check-then-act sequence with an unclosed TOCTOU window — the same race class the incident describes, where the ownership check ran 39s after another session had already advanced current_revision. Confirming current_revision before calling submit does not make the submit atomic with respect to a concurrent upload that lands between the check and the submit call.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria, line 2 ('A submit is refused... when the current_revision differs from the revision whose votes were inspected')
findings.suggested_fix: Require the submit to pass the inspected revision-id to Gerrit's submit endpoint (which rejects if it is no longer current), making the guard atomic rather than a separate read-then-submit.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the ownership check must not rely solely on machine-local state (registry file / `git worktree list`), or scope its guarantee explicitly to same-host sessions and name what the check does when sessions run on separate hosts under the shared identity.
evidence: Plan direction: 'A machine-local claim registry mapping change number -> worktree/session'
AC1: 'check git worktree list for a local holder before amending'
Matrix cell: Harness=remote MCP; Project location=server outside the checkout — no shared-local-filesystem assumption allowed
findings.finding: The 'machine-local claim registry' and the 'git worktree list' local-holder check assume all competing sessions share one host and local filesystem. In the remote-MCP / server-outside-the-checkout shape, concurrent sessions can run on different hosts under the same RebarBotNava identity; a per-host registry and a local worktree scan cannot observe another host's claim, so the ownership check silently returns 'no other owner' and the write-race proceeds undetected.
findings.location: Directions: 'A machine-local claim registry' and Acceptance criteria line 1 ('check git worktree list for a local holder')
scenarios: Remote MCP / servers venue: two sessions on separate hosts share the RebarBotNava identity; the machine-local registry on host A never sees host B's claim, and `git worktree list` on host A never lists host B's worktree — the pre-submit check reports no concurrent owner and the competing patch set is pushed anyway.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Strengthen AC#2 (and Direction 3) to require the submit itself be atomically guarded against a competing patch set — e.g. mandate a revision-scoped submit that the server refuses when the inspected revision is no longer current (HTTP 409) — rather than only a client-side current_revision compare, and prove the refusal fires when a NEW patch set lands between inspection and submit (not merely against a pre-staled revision).
evidence: AC#2: 'A submit is refused, or at minimum loudly warned, when the current_revision differs from the revision whose votes were inspected. Proven by attempting a submit against a deliberately stale revision and observing the refusal.'
Direction 3: 'confirm current_revision matches what you inspected, confirm votes are live rather than Outdated'
The ticket's premise is a race resolved in 39 seconds (PS4 uploaded 02:35:39, check ran 02:36:18) — a client-side compare done at inspection time has an identical window before the submit call.

ABSENCE: the plan text nowhere states the submit must be revision-scoped/atomic (server-side rejection of a stale revision), only that the client should compare current_revision — a check-then-act TOCTOU.
findings.finding: The pre-submit ownership/staleness check specified in AC#2 and Direction 3 is a client-side compare-then-submit ("confirm current_revision matches what you inspected"), which is itself a check-then-act with a race window between the inspection and the submit POST — the same 39-second window the ticket is built to eliminate. The plan does not require the submit itself to be atomically guarded against a competing patch set (e.g. a revision-scoped submit the server rejects when the revision is no longer current), so a compliant implementation could still lose a race that lands between the compare and the submit.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria, AC line 2 ("A submit is refused ... when the current_revision differs from the revision whose votes were inspected") and Directions bullet 3 ("confirm current_revision matches what you inspected")
scenarios: Session A inspects current_revision = X and its live votes, the compare passes; before A's submit lands, Session B uploads patch set X+1; A's submit either lands stale state or, if not revision-scoped, competes anyway.
An implementer satisfies AC#2 with a plain GET-compare followed by a generic (non-revision-scoped) submit call and passes the deliberately-stale test while still leaving the live race open.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword AC#2 to: 'A submit is issued against the specific inspected revision (revision-scoped submit) and is refused by the server when that revision is no longer current; proven by uploading a competing patch set AFTER inspection and before submit and observing the refusal (HTTP 409), not merely by submitting a pre-staled revision.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Note Gerrit's revision-scoped submit endpoint (POST /changes/{id}/revisions/{revision-id}/submit, which refuses a non-current revision) as prior art for AC #2, and state whether the chosen guard uses it or a client-side check and why.
evidence: Retrieved: Gerrit Code Review /changes/ REST API (gerrit-review.googlesource.com) documents a revision-scoped 'Submit Revision' endpoint POST /changes/{change-id}/revisions/{revision-id}/submit
Plan AC #2: 'A submit is refused, or at minimum loudly warned, when the current_revision differs from the revision whose votes were inspected'
Plan proposes to 'document (and script)' a bespoke pre-submit verification without referencing Gerrit's own revision-scoped submit guard
ABSENCE: no mention anywhere in the plan of Gerrit's native behavior when submitting a non-current revision
findings.finding: AC #2's stale-revision submit guard has directly relevant Gerrit-native prior art the plan does not consider: Gerrit's submit REST endpoint is revision-scoped (POST /changes/{id}/revisions/{revision-id}/submit) and refuses to submit a revision that is not current, which is nearly the exact guard the plan proposes to script.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria, item 2 ('A submit is refused ... when the current_revision differs ...') and 'Directions' third bullet
scenarios: Author scripts a client-side current_revision comparison that duplicates a guard Gerrit already enforces server-side when submit is addressed to a specific revision
A future implementer submits by change-id ('current') and re-introduces the race the revision-scoped endpoint would have prevented
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to AC #2 / the third Direction pinning the submit to the inspected revision-id via the revision-scoped submit endpoint (so Gerrit rejects a stale submit atomically), and justify any additional client-side check on top of it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Frame the revision-match pre-submit check as optimistic concurrency control (read a version token, reject the write on mismatch) and acknowledge the residual TOCTOU window between inspection and submit.
evidence: Retrieved: 'Optimistic concurrency control' (Wikipedia) and 'Optimistic Concurrency with SQL Version Columns' describe carrying a revision/version token from read to write and treating a failed match as a conflict
Plan describes 'confirm current_revision matches what you inspected' as a discovered-by-luck procedure rather than an instance of a named pattern
ABSENCE: no reference to optimistic-locking / version-token / CAS terminology
findings.finding: The plan's core mechanism — carry the inspected revision forward and reject the write on mismatch — is the established optimistic-concurrency-control / compare-and-swap pattern, but the plan describes it in bespoke terms without naming or referencing the prior art, so its novelty (if any) is not distinguished from the standard approach.
findings.location: 'Why it is worth fixing' and 'Directions' third bullet; AC #2
scenarios: Reviewer or implementer cannot quickly map the proposed check to a known correctness model and its known failure modes (e.g. TOCTOU window between inspection and submit)
